passages.title: Vashti refuses the king
passages.summary: Ahasuerus holds large feasts. Vashti refuses his order to appear. Memucan urges him to replace her. One refusal becomes a rule for every household. The king’s advisers fear women following Vashti’s example.
passages.uncertainty: Susa marks the story’s setting. Individual rooms and courier roads are not mapped.

lds.text: The Seminary lesson starts with the king’s decision to replace Vashti.

passages.title: Esther becomes queen
passages.summary: Hegai helps Esther in the women’s house. Ahasuerus chooses her as queen. Mordecai reports a plot against him. Esther keeps her people and family secret. The report of Mordecai’s help enters the king’s records.
passages.uncertainty: Jerusalem and Babylon belong to the earlier family account. The palace story takes place in Susa.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me studies Mordecai’s care for Esther after her parents die.

passages.title: Haman orders the Jews’ deaths
passages.summary: Mordecai refuses to bow to Haman. Haman obtains the king’s ring and sends orders to kill all the Jews. Haman turns anger at one man against a whole people. Written orders spread the danger.
passages.uncertainty: Susa marks the story’s setting. Individual rooms and courier roads are not mapped.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me asks how Haman’s anger turns into danger for other people.

passages.title: Esther decides to approach the king
passages.summary: Hathach carries messages between Mordecai and Esther. Esther asks the Jews to fast before she risks approaching the king. The palace does not protect Esther from danger to her people. She asks others to share her preparation.
passages.uncertainty: Susa marks the story’s setting. Individual rooms and courier roads are not mapped.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me connects Esther’s decision with courage and fasting before difficult choices.

passages.title: Two invitations and Haman’s anger
passages.summary: The king receives Esther. She invites him and Haman to two meals. Zeresh suggests preparing a gallows for Mordecai. Haman’s honors cannot satisfy him while Mordecai refuses to bow. His friends strengthen his plan.
passages.uncertainty: Susa marks the story’s setting. Individual rooms and courier roads are not mapped.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me compares Esther’s risk with Haman’s pride and anger.

passages.title: Haman must honor Mordecai
passages.summary: The king hears how Mordecai saved him. Haman must lead Mordecai through the city with royal clothing and a horse. Haman expects honor for himself. Instead, he must praise the man he wants to kill.
passages.uncertainty: Susa marks the story’s setting. Individual rooms and courier roads are not mapped.

lds.text: The Seminary lesson recalls how the king’s records bring Mordecai’s service back into view.

passages.title: Esther names Haman as the enemy
passages.summary: Esther asks for her life and her people’s lives. She names Haman. Harbonah points out the gallows, and Haman dies. Esther connects the threat to herself before naming its author. The king turns against Haman.
passages.uncertainty: Susa marks the story’s setting. Individual rooms and courier roads are not mapped.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me asks what Haman’s choices reveal about his motives and their results.

passages.title: New orders allow the Jews to fight
passages.summary: Esther asks again for her people. Mordecai receives the king’s ring. New letters permit the Jews to gather and fight attackers. Haman’s death does not cancel his letters. Esther keeps asking until new orders address the remaining danger.
passages.uncertainty: Susa marks the story’s setting. Individual rooms and courier roads are not mapped.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me links the new letters with its study of fasting during danger.

passages.title: Victory, violence, and Purim
passages.summary: The Jews kill their enemies without taking goods. Esther requests another day in Susa. Letters establish Purim with feasts and gifts. The days of fear become days of joy. Gifts to people in need become part of remembering.
passages.uncertainty: Susa marks the story’s setting. Individual rooms and courier roads are not mapped.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me connects Esther’s courage with the later days of gladness.

passages.title: Mordecai serves his people
passages.summary: Ahasuerus collects payment from his lands. Mordecai holds high office and works for his people’s good. Mordecai’s lasting importance comes from helping his people, beyond the honor he receives.
passages.uncertainty: Susa marks the story’s setting. Individual rooms and courier roads are not mapped.

lds.text: Mordecai works for his people’s good. Who benefits from the authority he receives?
